doc.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The 1965 Japan tour with Jackie McLean, Freddie Hubbard and Roy Haynes
summary: After the Jazztet, Golson was composing and gigging; he lists the all-star band on the tour of Japan and praises Freddie Hubbard and Roy Haynes.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah, but we all knew him when he came to New York with Jon Hendricks, and then he just took off quickly. But he landed that money gig. What can you say? So, the Jazztet ’62. At this point you’re making your living as a composer-arranger.
And gigging. The next thing that appears was the tour to Japan with Jackie McLean in ’65.
I see that big smile on your face.

That was something. Kenny Dorham, Freddie Hubbard, Jackie McLean, Benny Golson, Cedar Walton, Reggie Workman, and Roy Haynes. Boy, that was something. But Kenny was – Freddie was playing so much. I said, oh, I feel sorry for Kenny Dorham. Boy, this guy. It was unreal. And Roy Haynes, the consummate drummer. The chronology means absolutely nothing to him. I said to him, “Where do you hide your portrait?”, like Dorian Gray. The portrait gets old, but he doesn’t get old. I went to hear him at the Blue Note in New York about three years ago. He’s 80-something then. He played like a high-school kid. Yeah, I didn’t mention him: Art Blakey, Kenny Clarke, and Roy Haynes. Incredible. He can tip.
